clue.text: Fine print a delight

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for an adjective meaning delightful or attractive

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
an etching is a print taken from an engraved plate

explanation.surface: A collector admires a finely made print, calling it a delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine print' looks like the small type in a contract, but it splits into F and a kind of print.
explanation.definitionFit: Something attractive and charming is a delight to look at, the sense of the adjective in 'a fetching hat'.

clue.text: Champion loses round — squashed by Big Daddy

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece lies under, squashed by, the other

parts.note: big and fat are near synonyms for large

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away from the word

parts.note: a hero is a champion
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A wrestling champion loses a bout, flattened by Big Daddy, the famous British wrestler.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Daddy was a hugely popular heavyweight on British television wrestling. Here 'Big' and 'Daddy' are split.
explanation.definitionFit: Daddy is a child's word for one's male parent.

clue.text: Old slinger, English, bowled in windy Utrecht

indicators.note: windy suggests letters blown about and scattered

parts.note: B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: An English cricketer is bowled out in a blustery Dutch city.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval siege engine hurled heavy stones with a counterweighted arm, an old catapult or slinger.

clue.text: Measure causing runner in field to receive shocking treatment

indicators.note: one piece receives the other inside it

parts.note: a hare runs across open fields
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, an electric shock treatment

explanation.surface: A sprinter in a sports field gets an electric shock as a disciplinary measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner in field' sounds like an athlete but is an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This metric unit of 10,000 square metres is a measure of land area.

clue.text: In ammunition it replaced explosive component

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In making ammunition, this substance was swapped in for an explosive ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is a key ingredient of gunpowder, so it is a component of an explosive.

clue.text: Compassion from soldiers deployed in temple hospital

indicators.note: soldiers deployed in a place are stationed inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia
RM, the Royal Marines, are soldiers serving at sea
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Troops stationed at a temple hospital show compassion to the sick.
explanation.walkthrough: WAT is a Buddhist temple in Southeast Asia, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth of feeling is kindly sympathy, a near synonym of compassion.

clue.text: Sceptic is entertained by Hatter, not completely mad

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held within
mad signals letters going wild into a new order
not completely means the word is cut short by a letter

explanation.surface: A doubter is a guest at the Mad Hatter's tea party in Wonderland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hatter' evokes Lewis Carroll's mad tea party, but here it is just fodder: trimmed by 'not completely', then shuffled by 'mad', with 'is' held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A disbeliever in God is a religious sceptic.

clue.text: Author has knight appear in distance

indicators.note: the knight is made to appear inside the distance

parts.note: a mile is a measure of distance
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A writer has a knight show up some way off in his story.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne wrote Winnie-the-Pooh, so he is a well-known author.

clue.text: One on vacation not over the top in making punch

indicators.note: not here means without, so these letters are left out

parts.note: a tourist or vacationer is a holidaymaker
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a lid is the top of a pot or box

explanation.surface: A tourist, restrained for once, mixes a holiday punch without going overboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not over the top' looks like 'restrained' but removes O and LID. 'in making' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild, swinging blow in boxing is called this, a type of punch.

clue.text: Bomb outside church planted by sanctimonious tart

indicators.note: the bomb goes outside the other pieces

parts.note: a mine is a buried bomb

indicators.note: the church is set down next to the next piece

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
pi is slang for pious or sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A bomb outside a church was planted by a self-righteous loose woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like an insult for a woman but means a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: The small Christmas pastry filled with dried fruit is a kind of tart.

clue.text: With husband in supermarket, this aptly represented 25 ac

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 25 across, a play by Shakespeare

indicators.note: the husband is placed inside the supermarket's name

parts.note: Tesco is the largest British supermarket chain
H is the abbreviation for husband, as in genealogies

indicators.note: represented here means presented again in a new arrangement, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A shopper with her husband in a supermarket finds that 'this' neatly stands for a famous play.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesco is a British supermarket chain; 'in' puts H inside it. 'represented' rearranges THIS APTLY into TTISHPLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre superstition forbids naming Shakespeare's Macbeth backstage, so actors use this euphemism instead.

clue.text: Train ferries coin between terminals at Stoke and Carlisle

indicators.note: to ferry is to carry, so the outer letters carry the coin within them
the coin sits between the two end letters picked out
the terminals of each place name are their final letters

parts.note: a ducat is an old gold coin used across Europe

explanation.surface: A railway ferry service carries coin between stations at Stoke and Carlisle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway noun but is the verb meaning teach. 'terminals at' takes the last letters, E and E, of Stoke and Carlisle.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone is to teach or instruct them, the same sense as to school or educate.

clue.text: Lion-headed monster to agree with hawk-headed god

parts.note: to chime with something is to agree or harmonise with it
Ra, the Egyptian sun god, is shown with a falcon's head

explanation.surface: A mythological mix-up: a lion-headed beast finds common ground with a hawk-headed deity.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the fire-breathing beast slain by Bellerophon had a lion's head, goat's body and serpent's tail.

clue.text: Vergers in Eastbridge paid to board vessel — Suffolk submerged here?

definitions.note: a Suffolk is a breed of sheep, dunked in a bath of insecticide

indicators.note: to board a ship is to go inside it, so these letters go within the vessel

parts.note: a ship is a sea-going vessel

indicators.note: the verges, or edges, of the word are its outer letters

parts.note: PD is the usual abbreviation for paid, as stamped on a bill

explanation.surface: Church vergers in a Suffolk village pay to board a boat, then the county sinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vergers in' (probably meant as 'Verges in') takes the edges of Eastbridge, E and E. Eastbridge is a Suffolk village; Suffolk is also a sheep breed, which is the real sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers drive sheep through a trough of disinfectant, so a breed like the Suffolk is plunged into it.

clue.text: Greek character celebrated in return, having set off

indicators.note: in return means read backwards

parts.note: eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet
noted means famous or celebrated

explanation.surface: A famous Greek figure is honoured on returning home after setting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' reverses both pieces together, ETA NOTED read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb or charge is to explode it, the transitive sense of the verb.

clue.text: Sporting supporter holds record in home of the brave

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a golf tee supports the ball before a drive
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A sports fan clutches a record in America, the 'home of the brave' of the anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home of the brave' recalls the US anthem, but 'brave' here is a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a Native American warrior, and the conical tent of the Plains peoples was his dwelling.

clue.text: Tried with Conservative to answer Liberal French citizen

parts.note: proven means tried and tested

explanation.surface: A French citizen is put on trial, with a Tory to answer a Liberal politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Provence in southern France is a French citizen.

clue.text: Pot allows one to be free from pain under cheek

indicators.note: in a down clue this piece goes below the other

parts.note: sauce is old slang for cheek or impudence

indicators.note: being free from something means it is removed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Pot smoking lets a person escape pain, though it comes with cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' suggests cannabis, but it is a cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep cooking vessel with a long handle is a pot.

clue.text: Soon is about time for this man

definitions.note: a man's first name is wanted

indicators.note: one word is placed around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon or shortly

explanation.surface: Someone's time is nearly up: soon it will be this man's turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton is a man's given name, as in Chekhov, so the definition simply points to some man.

clue.text: Write uplifting melody for part of musical work

indicators.note: uplifting in a down clue means the letters read upwards

parts.note: to pen is to write
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: A composer writes a soaring melody for one movement of a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Holst's suite The Planets has a movement for this planet, so it is part of a musical work.

clue.text: Alpine heroine in child's book

indicators.note: the heroine is placed inside the child

parts.note: a tot is a small child
Heidi is the girl of Johanna Spyri's novel set in the Swiss Alps

explanation.surface: The girl from the Alps appears in a children's book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'child's book' looks like one phrase describing Heidi itself, but 'book' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Dostoevsky's novel about Prince Myshkin bears this title, so it is a famous book.

clue.text: Say no to failure

definitions.meaning: to refuse or turn down an offer
a gradual deterioration or falling off in health or strength

explanation.surface: A slogan urging people to refuse to accept defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both turning down an invitation and a falling-away or deterioration.

clue.text: Getting closer to pheasant in hunting land is simple

indicators.note: the picked letter goes inside the hunting land

parts.note: a chase is an unenclosed tract of land kept for hunting, as in Cannock Chase

indicators.note: the closer of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A hunter getting near a pheasant in the shooting grounds finds it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: A chase is a British term for old hunting land.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste can describe a plain, unadorned style, so it is a synonym of simple.

clue.text: Study about swindle produces article that's spiked

indicators.note: the study goes round the swindle

parts.note: to con is to study or pore over something
a ramp is British slang for a swindle or racket

explanation.surface: Research into a fraud yields a newspaper article that the editor kills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spiked' suggests a rejected news story, but it means fitted with metal points.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers strap a frame of metal points to their boots for gripping ice, an article with spikes.

clue.text: Lucky creature, heading off for prestigious meeting

indicators.note: with its heading off the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a mascot is an animal or figure kept to bring luck

explanation.surface: A lucky charm animal sets off for an important event.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Ascot is a fashionable horse-race meeting in Berkshire, England, a prestigious social occasion.

clue.text: Mother caught with Hebrew character in bloody drama

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
beth is the second letter of the Hebrew alphabet

explanation.surface: A mother is caught up with a Hebrew letter in some violent play.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy of a murderous Scottish king is soaked in killings, a famously gory play.

clue.text: Nonsense marks end to scholarly attention

parts.note: M abbreviates marks, the former German currency

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: to keep an eye on something is to pay it attention

explanation.surface: A teacher's marks show the scholar's attention ran out at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is old-fashioned slang for rubbish or I don't believe it.

clue.text: Salvage relationship — and what's left of crockery!

definitions.meaning: to restore things after a break-up or crisis
literally gathering broken shards of a smashed plate

explanation.surface: After a row with plates thrown, a couple tries to mend things and sweep up.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for recovering after a disaster is taken literally as gathering the fragments of broken china.

clue.text: Eccentric person for example gets married in tree

parts.note: a nut is a crank or eccentric
eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: An oddball gets married up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Indian evergreen whose seed gives the spice is a tree of the same name.

clue.text: Troops at glen heard bugle call

indicators.note: heard means the words are taken as spoken, matching in pronunciation

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are troops, and a glen is a valley; together they make the phrase said aloud

explanation.surface: Soldiers camped in a Scottish glen hear the morning bugle.
explanation.walkthrough: The British pronunciation ri-VAL-ee is needed; Americans say REV-uh-lee.
explanation.definitionFit: The bugle signal that wakes soldiers in the morning is this call.
